Package with both a library and a binary?Ask a questionAsked 3 years ago · Active 5 months ago · Seen 12k timesVotes: 42

I want one Rust package that holds a library with most of the logic, and a small binary that calls it, so that other projects can use the library while I still ship a command line tool.

If I read the module docs right, both can live in one package. What should myCargo.tomlfile look like, and where do the two source files go?

  • rust-cargo

Yes. Cargo builds a library from the lib file and a binary from the bin file of the same package; the layout below is all you need.

$ ls -R
Cargo.toml src/lib.rs src/main.rs

Cargo.toml:

[package]
name = "mything"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[lib]
name = "mylib"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "mybin"
path = "src/main.rs"

src/lib.rs:

pub fn greet() { println!("Hello from the library"); }

src/main.rs:

use mylib::greet;
fn main() { greet(); }

With the default paths you can even leave both tables out: a lib file and a main file in the same source folder are found on their own, and the binary takes the package name.

One more thing to know: the binary only sees the public items of the library, the same way any other package would, so keep the binary small and put the logic you want to test in the library. Integration tests in the tests folder can then call the library directly.
